STEP 2 - Ruler: White oval paper plate, roughly 20 cm long by about 15 cm wide at the widest visible point. Treating it as a side-size plate, diameter ~20 cm, area = 3.14 x 10^2 ≈ 314 cm^2 (small plate, slight angle makes it look oval).

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked bacon strips (two to three pieces, partly overlapping), with some grease/reddish residue on the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon pieces are thin, flattened, about 0.6 cm thick on average in the pile. 38 cm^2 x 0.6 cm ≈ 23 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 23 ml x 0.95 bulk density ≈ 22 g of cooked bacon.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g. 22 g x 5.4 ≈ 119 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two to three cooked bacon strips weigh roughly 15–25 g and about 80–150 kcal, which matches. Total plausible.

Summary: about 22 g of cooked bacon, roughly 120 kcal.
